summary: This September 15, 2023 article outlines cloud security measures remote teams can use to protect sensitive information. It covers secure cloud infrastructure, identity and access management, encryption, patch management, endpoint security, training, response plans and regular audits, supported by quotes from various security experts. It concludes that organizations should build an ongoing culture of cybersecurity vigilance.
one_line: Overview of key cloud security practices for remote teams, including IAM, encryption, patching, endpoint security, training, response plans and audits.
key_facts: The article, dated September 15, 2023, argues that cloud security is crucial as remote teams access company data from various locations and often on personal devices.
James Martins of SecureTech Innovations says "87% of companies rely on the cloud for their day-to-day operations."

John Smith, CTO of NextGen Security, advises choosing cloud providers with robust security practices, including regular data encryption, strong network protections and a transparent data-handling policy.
Ashley Rodriguez, head of IT at CyberSecure Inc., said multi-factor authentication and strict access controls reduced unauthorized breach risk by over 60% in the past year.
Identity and Access Management (IAM) tools control who may access what information, with access tailored to roles and responsibilities.
Encrypting data in transit and at rest makes it unreadable without the decryption key; Tanya Vasquez of DataGuard calls encryption "like a deadbolt for your data."
Mike Chen of CloudSafe Solutions says "An unpatched system is an open invitation for threat actors" and that automated patch management is a necessity for dispersed remote teams.
Peter Thomson, a remote work security coordinator, says endpoint security tools such as antivirus software and mobile device management track every device connecting to the network.
Sophia Lee of e-SecureTrain says regular training helps employees identify and respond to threats and instills collective responsibility for cybersecurity.
Luke Patterson, CEO of ResponseReady, says a response plan maps out clear roles and responsibilities, communication channels and recovery steps.
Diana Clarke of AuditMaster Tech says periodic assessments give an objective view of security standing and help adjust strategies to new threats.
The article concludes that companies should create an ongoing culture of cybersecurity vigilance.
